classification.description: Demolition, site preparation and clearance work

tender.description:
Removal of eight boilers and ancillary equipment, including demolition of buildings and safe removal of hazards such as asbestos containing materials.

See full description and Scope document for full details.

lots.description:
Dungeness ‘A’ is a redundant nuclear power station located on the Romney Marsh in Kent. The power station ceased generation in 2006 and is currently undergoing decommissioning.

The scope of works is for the Contractor to undertake the role of “Principal Contractor” for the safe removal of all hazards including Asbestos Containing Materials (ACM’s), soft stripping internal fixtures, fittings & linings and removal of the Boilers, by pass ducts, main gas duct sections, suitable laydown and weatherproof storage. The safe demolition of the buildings adjoining the east and west faces of the reactor buildings of the Dungeness A Site, noting the Blower Halls and Central Control Block are reduced to slab level with other buildings reduced as stated in the scope of works and in accordance with BS6187:2011 Code of Practice for Full and Partial Demolition (Ref. 16.4.1).

To provide some idea of scale, Dungeness has eight boilers which will require removal and laydown. These are estimated at 7m in diameter and 21m long, they weigh approximately 700 tonnes each. Approximately 30% of the building structures currently on Site will be removed by the contract.

The Employer will apply for any necessary planning permissions and carry out any activities necessary to obtain the Planning Approval. The Contractor is to provide all management, documentation, labour, plant, equipment, and materials to remove the hazards, de-plant all equipment, lifting and removal of the Boilers, by pass ducts, main gas duct sections, suitable laydown and weatherproof storage, demolition of the buildings and make good weatherproof of remaining structures including site remediation.

The scope of this project includes the preparation and execution of all necessary investigation work such as ground, geological, ordnance, camera, flow surveys, etc. necessary to complete the scope of works.

This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice.  
Representations by providers must be made to the relevant authority by 19 November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.  Please email procurement.wellbeing@bcpcouncil.gov.uk  if you have any enquiries.
The award decision was made jointly by Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council and Dorset Council following assessment by an evaluation panel . 
All individuals involved in the assessment and award decision were required to declare any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest prior to participating in the evaluation process. No conflicts of interest were identified that would have affected the integrity of the assessment process.
The authorities assessed providers against the key criteria set out within the Provider Selection Regime, giving greatest importance to the provider's ability to deliver safe, effective and high-quality sexual health services that meet the needs of the population across Bournemouth, Christchurch, Poole and Dorset.
The relative importance of the key criteria reflected the strategic objectives of the service and the requirement to ensure continuity of care, improved health outcomes, accessibility, integration with wider health and care services, value for money and social value. Clinical quality, service delivery capability and population health outcomes were considered of higher importance than cost considerations due to the critical nature of the service and the need to maintain safe and effective provision.
The selected provider was considered to offer the most advantageous solution when assessed against the key criteria. The provider demonstrated a strong track record of delivering integrated sexual health services, evidenced high levels of clinical quality and patient outcomes, robust arrangements for partnership working across the local health system, and the capacity and capability required to meet current and future service requirements. The authorities were satisfied that the provider represented the most suitable provider in accordance with the Provider Selection Regime.
The authorities gave greatest importance to Quality and Innovation (40%), Value for Money (30%), Integration, Collaboration and Sustainability (10%), Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice (10%) and Social Value (10%). The relative weightings reflected the need to secure high-quality, accessible and integrated sexual health services whilst ensuring sustainability and value for money. The successful provider achieved the highest overall assessment, particularly in respect of quality, clinical outcomes, accessibility and integration with wider health and care services.

The service will be awarded as a single contract and will not be divided into lots. 
The service shall deliver: 
• Sexual health prevention, testing, diagnosis and treatment services. 
• Reproductive health and contraception services, including Long Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC). 
• HIV testing, prevention and Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) services. 
• Digital and self-managed sexual health pathways, including online information, triage and home testing where clinically appropriate.

• Clinical outreach services designed to improve access and reduce health inequalities. 
• Services for children and young people. 
• Workforce development, training and public health prevention initiatives. 
The provider will be expected to deliver a blended model of care comprising: 
• Face-to-face clinical services, (CQC Registration requirement - Level Good or above) 
• Telephone consultations. 
• Digital access routes and online service provision. 
• Walk-in services where appropriate. 
• Same-day assessment pathways for urgent clinical need. 
• Integrated pathways enabling seamless movement between digital, telephone and in-person services. 
The contract is intended to secure a single provider capable of delivering accessible, high-quality, person-centred services across both council areas, ensuring continuity of care and consistent service standards throughout the contract term.

lots.description:
New requirement - replacement of Brighton Recovery College (C363540), and the SPFT in-House provided Recovery College.

Currently the pan-Sussex Recovery college is provided by two Providers. Brighton is provided by Southdown, previously contracted directly by NHS Sussex but recently delegated to SPFT under the delegated commissioning processes/agenda. The remainder has been provided by SPFT for many years.

The provision across Sussex is being re-designed to provide a single comprehensive prospectus of courses for all students regardless of where they live in Sussex. The prospectus will provide participants with a variety of learning opportunities that align with their recovery goals and proactively tackle health inequalities, and support individuals at the highest risk of marginalization.

The service will be delivered by SPFT in conjunction with a VCSE organisation.

SPFT courses will be co-delivered with clinicians / mental health practitioners. Some are aimed at students with more complex needs but also include understanding and managing common conditions. Courses will be accessible for people recently discharged from hospital or in crisis, focusing on understanding diagnosis and navigating services.

VCSE courses will offer further learning around maintaining recovery, including wellbeing and creative courses. Courses will have a strong link to community networks, some through sub partnerships with charities and community organisations. These courses will respond to local population needs (health inequalities) and focus on moving away from services to volunteering, getting back to work or study

tender.title: Winter Access Hubs Service for Bromley
tender.description:
This notice is an intention to award a contract under the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) process (The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 10). 
NHS South East London Integrated Care Board (SEL ICB) is seeking to commission a Winter Access Hubs Service to provide additional same-day primary care capacity for Bromley residents during periods of seasonal demand and winter system pressures.
The service will deliver timely assessment and treatment for patients requiring urgent same-day primary care access through a geographically distributed network of hub locations across Bromley. The service is intended to support general practice, urgent care and acute services by managing appropriate patients within primary care settings and reducing avoidable attendances at Urgent Treatment Centres and Emergency Departments.
Key features of the service include:
•Provision of additional same-day GP-led capacity for winter illness and other urgent primary care presentations.
•Delivery of predominantly face-to-face consultations through convenient hub locations across the borough.
•Direct booking and referral pathways from General Practice, NHS 111 and Urgent Treatment Centres.
•Integration with community pharmacy, self-referral pathways and wider neighbourhood services to ensure patients receive care in the most appropriate setting.
•Flexible deployment of capacity in response to emerging winter demand and system pressures.
•Use of shared digital solutions and GP clinical systems to support integrated patient care and continuity of information.
•Collection and reporting of activity, utilisation, patient outcomes and service impact data to support ongoing service evaluation and improvement.
The service forms part of Bromley's winter resilience arrangements and aims to improve access to urgent primary care, reduce pressure on urgent and emergency care services, and support delivery of the NHS objective of providing timely same-day assessment in community settings.
This is a 3 months contract (subject to change).

lots.description:
The notice relates to the provision of a Winter Access Hubs Service for patients registered with a Bromley GP practice.
The commissioner is seeking a provider capable of delivering a resilient, responsive and integrated same-day primary care service throughout the winter period, supporting both in-hours and out-of-hours demand and operating as a key component of Bromley's winter resilience plan.
Under the contract, the provider will be expected to:
•Deliver approximately 7,000 additional same-day primary care appointments throughout the winter operational period (Dec 26 - Jan/Feb 27).
•Operate a network of accessible hub locations distributed across the four Bromley Integrated Neighbourhood Team footprints.
•Provide predominantly face-to-face consultations delivered by appropriately qualified General Practitioners.
•Accept and manage referrals from General Practice following clinical triage, together with referrals from NHS 111 and Urgent Treatment Centres.
•Ensure all clinically urgent patients are assessed on the same day where appropriate.
•Maintain sufficient resilience, workforce capacity and business continuity arrangements to respond to fluctuations in demand and winter pressures.
•Support appropriate utilisation of community pharmacy, self-care, self-referral pathways and wider primary care services to maximise the effectiveness of the service.
•Utilise EMIS and associated NHS digital systems to facilitate consultation recording, referral management and consultation write-back to registered GP practices.
•Undertake quality assurance, clinical audit and service evaluation activities to support continuous improvement and demonstrate impact on system performanceThe provider must demonstrate:
a) Experience of delivering large-scale same-day primary care services in Bromley.
b) The ability to mobilise and operate services across multiple locations in Bromley.
c) Effective relationships with Bromley General Practice, Primary Care Networks and urgent care partners.
d) Robust clinical governance, safeguarding and information governance arrangements.
e) The capability to work flexibly with commissioners to adjust capacity and service delivery in response to changing patterns of demand
f) Access to Bromley healthcare estate to support provision of the service.
The provider will be expected to work collaboratively with Bromley General Practices, Primary Care Networks, NHS 111, Urgent Treatment Centres, Community Pharmacy providers and other health and care partners to maximise utilisation of the service and support whole-system management of winter pressures.
The commissioner is seeking to achieve, through this procurement, a service that supports neighbourhood-based models of care, delivers rapid access to same-day primary care assessment, improves patient flow across the urgent and emergency care system, and contributes to reducing avoidable demand on General Practice, Urgent Treatment Centres and Emergency Departments during periods of peak winter pressure. The service will be expected to work as an integrated component of Bromley's wider winter resilience arrangements, supporting residents to receive the right care, at the right time, in the most appropriate setting while improving outcomes and delivering value for the local health and care system.
The process being followed is a Most Suitable Provider Process under the Provider Selection Regime 2023. Additional information: Relative Importance of Key Criteria:
The following key criteria were applied in the assessment of the provider:
- Quality and Innovation
- Value
- Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability
- Improving Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice
- Social Value
Rationale for the Relative Importance of the Key Criteria:
The relative importance of the key criteria reflects the Authority's need to secure a safe, high-quality, and effective service for patients with a provider that is committed to supporting the development of neighbourhood models of healthcare while ensuring value for money under the Provider Selection Regime. The assessment method of all five key criteria aimed to allow the Authority to identify the most suitable provider to achieve the service aims of improving wellbeing, increasing independence, and reducing avoidable reliance on urgent and acute services.

For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015/Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award. The publication of this notice marks the start of the standstill period. Representations by providers must be made to decision makers by 18 November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR Wales.
Representations by providers must be made by email to Michael.Groves@wales.nhs.uk.
The award decision-makers for this process are the Operational Team within the Mental Health Clinical Board of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board.
In accordance with the Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025, the Authority considered the provider's ability to deliver the service, maintain continuity of provision, support service user and carer engagement, facilitate effective partnership working across statutory and third sector organisations, and minimise disruption to vulnerable individuals accessing mental health support services.
The Authority considered these criteria to be of particular importance given the service's reliance on established relationships, stakeholder confidence and effective collaboration across statutory and voluntary sector organisations. Particular consideration was given to continuity of service delivery, maintenance of existing networks and engagement structures, local knowledge, and the potential impact of any change of provider on service users, carers and partner organisations.
The Authority is satisfied that the provider is capable of continuing to deliver the service and achieving the required outcomes. In reaching this decision, the Authority considered the provider's established relationships with service users, carers and stakeholders, experience of delivering the service, and ability to maintain continuity of provision.
The Authority noted that previous changes in provider arrangements had adversely affected service user and carer liaison functions and that significant effort had been required by Adferiad/Caniad to re-establish these workstreams and achieve high levels of participation and engagement. The Authority also considered the provider's established working relationship with the University Health Board Recovery College, including provision of a safe and familiar environment for service users, together with its role in administering the service user and carer reward and recognition programme.
The Authority concluded that the existing provider is suitable to continue delivering the service and that awarding the contract to that provider will support continuity of service delivery, maintain established stakeholder relationships, avoid unnecessary disruption to service users and carers, and continue to deliver positive outcomes.
No providers were excluded from the procurement process.
The contract was not awarded to an excluded provider.
All individuals involved in the evaluation and award decision were required to declare any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. No actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest were identified. Accordingly, no conflict management measures were required.

The service will operate as a strategic and operational link between the Health Board, third sector organisations, service users, carers and wider stakeholders involved in the planning, delivery and development of mental health services across Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan.

releases.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to decision makers by midnight on Wednesday the 18th November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.
Written representations should be sent to donna.iley@durham.gov.uk
Officers of Public Health Senior Management Team and Adult and Health Senior Management were the decision makers.
There were no Conflicts of interest identified among the Decision Makers.
The council has fully considered each of the key criteria when making a decision on the award of this contract. A particular emphasis was placed upon:
Key criterion 1: Quality and innovation
HDFT consistently delivers strong performance across the 0-25 Family Health Service. Robust governance and data-quality arrangements are in place. Quality and safety remain strong, with routine monitoring of incidents and complaints, low levels of formal escalation and consistently positive service-user feedback. HDFT continues to invest in quality improvement, supporting service development, evaluation and continuous improvement. 
Key criterion 2: Value
The service supports over 150,000 children and young people, providing universal and targeted support in response to significant levels of need and health inequality across County Durham. HDFT demonstrates financial responsibility through transparent monthly reporting on staffing and workforce pressures and has reduced its management fee over the contract term, supporting continued cost efficiency.
Key criterion 3: Integration, collaboration and service sustainability
HDFT works effectively with Public Health, Early Help, Children's Social Care, Maternity Services and Family Hubs, supporting integrated pathways and a consistent "no wrong door" approach for families.
HDFT responds collaboratively to system change and emerging need through joint pathways, strengthened referral arrangements and active participation in strategic public health partnerships.
Key criterion 4: Access, inequalities and choice
HDFT supports access and reduces inequalities through a tiered model of universal, enhanced and targeted provision, enabling early identification of need and preventative support.
Services are delivered flexibly across homes, community venues, Family Hubs and schools, supported by digital provision including a 24/7 health app, online resources and practitioner-led health chat.
Key criterion 5: Social value
HDFT has exceeded social value expectations through local employment, apprenticeship learning and volunteering activity, supporting local workforce and community development.

tender.title: CHS - Acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) Contract Extension
tender.description:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust intends to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system for a further three years, with an option to extend for an additional 12 months.

The extension will maintain continuity of the Trust’s existing clinical digital services, including the core EPR software, application management, hosting and associated support services. The existing system is integral to the Trust's clinical workflows and digital infrastructure, with significant technical dependencies and integration requirements.

The proposed arrangements include the removal of certain existing functionality and the introduction of additional integrated functionality, including Blood Transfusion Administration and Milk Management modules, to support the Trust's clinical and operational requirements. These modules require integration with the existing EPR environment, making technical compatibility, interoperability and continuity of clinical services key considerations.

The Trust is also progressing plans for a future competitive procurement of its EPR requirements, with the proposed extension providing continuity of existing services during this period.

lots.description:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust proposes to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system, commencing on 29th December 2026 for an initial period of three years, with an option to extend for a further 12 months.

The proposed arrangements cover the continued provision of the core EPR software and associated clinical applications, application management, hosting, software licensing, maintenance and technical support services. These services support the Trust's existing clinical and operational activities and the integration of the EPR with other systems across its digital infrastructure.

The proposed arrangements also incorporate changes to the existing scope, including the removal of certain voice recognition, in-application training and user guidance functionality. Additional requirements include increased system user capacity, enhanced application management support, upgrade management services, and further integrated clinical functionality supporting blood transfusion administration and milk management to meet the Trust's operational requirements. A trial of AI-enabled clinical functionality will also be included to evaluate its potential benefits and inform the Trust's future EPR requirements.

The existing EPR operates within a complex and highly integrated technical environment, with established interfaces, clinical workflows and dependencies across the Trust’s wider digital infrastructure. The additional functionality must operate effectively and safely within this environment, maintaining compatibility with the core EPR platform and associated clinical systems.

Introducing an alternative supplier at this stage would present significant technical and interoperability challenges, including the need for additional integration, configuration, testing, clinical safety assurance and ongoing support arrangements. This could create disproportionate technical difficulties and operational risks to established clinical services, alongside unnecessary duplication of implementation, integration and support costs. Continuing with the incumbent supplier will preserve compatibility with the existing EPR environment and enable the proposed requirements to be delivered through established technical and operational arrangements.

The proposed three-year extension, with an option for a further 12 months, reflects the complexity of maintaining and supporting a highly integrated clinical system while accommodating the Trust’s naturally evolving clinical and operational requirements. The optional fourth year recognises the complexity of a major clinical system procurement and transition, providing for circumstances where additional time may be required to complete implementation, data migration and associated integration activities while maintaining continuity of essential clinical services.

The Trust is separately progressing its longer-term EPR strategy, which will include a competitive procurement for its longer-term EPR requirements. The proposed extension is intended to maintain continuity of the existing EPR environment throughout the competitive procurement process, and support implementation and transition to the future arrangements.

The estimated total value of the proposed extension, including the optional fourth year, is approximately £17,549,439 excluding VAT.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust intends to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the continued provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system, on the grounds of technical compatibility, interoperability and the significant technical and operational difficulties associated with introducing an alternative supplier at this stage.

The existing Oracle Health EPR is an established and highly integrated clinical system, supporting essential patient care and operational activities across the Trust. It is embedded within clinical workflows and connected to other clinical and operational systems through established interfaces, data flows and supporting infrastructure. The continued operation of this environment requires compatibility between the core EPR platform, associated applications, hosting arrangements and ongoing application management and support services.

The current contract expires on 28th December 2026. Introducing an alternative EPR supplier within the remaining contractual period would require substantial technical and operational activity, including system configuration, development and testing of interfaces, data migration, validation, clinical safety assurance and the implementation of revised clinical workflows. These activities would need to be undertaken in a planned and controlled manner to protect the integrity and availability of patient information and maintain continuity of essential clinical services. It would not be practicable to complete such a transition before expiry of the existing arrangements.

The proposed extension also incorporates adjustments to the existing services, including additional user capacity, application management and upgrade management services, together with integrated clinical functionality - these requirements are closely connected to the existing EPR environment. Introducing alternative suppliers to deliver these elements separately would create additional technical dependencies and interoperability challenges, potentially requiring further interfaces, configuration, testing and separate support arrangements. Such an approach could result in disproportionate technical difficulties and significant economic inefficiencies, including duplication of implementation, integration, licensing and support costs. It could also necessitate maintaining parallel technical arrangements while the Trust continues to operate and support its existing EPR platform.

The proposed extension with Oracle Health will maintain continuity of the established EPR environment and enable the associated requirements to be delivered within the existing technical and operational arrangements, avoiding the disproportionate disruption and duplication of costs associated with introducing alternative provision at this stage.

The Trust is separately progressing its longer-term EPR strategy, which will include a competitive procurement for its future EPR requirements. The proposed extension is intended to maintain continuity of essential clinical services throughout that process and support implementation and transition to the future arrangements.

Provide accessible, confidential promotion, prevention and support services across both boroughs.

Improve integration and pathways with clinical sexual health providers, primary care, mental health, substance misuse and other key services.

tender.title: Provision of a Specialist Adult Substance Use Treatment Service 2027
tender.description:
This notice is for the award of a Substance Use Treatment Service under Direct Award Process C of the Provider Selection Regime.
This contract will replace the existing contract that expires on 31/03/2027.

lots.description:
The Authority intends to award a contract for the Service to the existing provider pursuant to Direct Award Process C under Regulation 9 of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 ("PSR").
This is a notice under Regulation 9 (3) of the Authority's intention to award the contract for the Service as described below to the existing provider.
North Somerset Council currently holds a contract with We Are With You (With you) to provide treatment and support for individuals affected by drugs and alcohol. 
The current service is a single provider model providing a combined drug and alcohol service predominately for adults, with where required, advice and prescribing for young people alongside the Council's Substance Advise Service (SAS). A broad range of interventions are available including; advice and information, needle and syringe provision, blood borne virus (BBV) testing and vaccinations, naloxone provision including a peer led delivery service, one to one psychosocial interventions, a range of group programmes, prescribing for opiate substitution therapy and alcohol withdrawal and stabilisation, community detoxification, mental health support, and access to medically assisted and managed detoxification and residential treatment.
The service performs well and exceeds many of the government ambitions including achieving a 17.5% increase in overall numbers in treatment over the last 4-years (44% increase in alcohol numbers and 27% increase in those using non-opiates). This is whilst maintaining an above national average for individuals making substantial progress in treatment. With You generally exceed national averages for engaging people in treatment within 3 weeks of leaving prison. Where engagement fluctuates and to address and alleviate issues With You's criminal justice team have developed a close working relationship with Prison and Probation services, including HMP Bristol.  
The new contract will commence on 1 April 2027, for a period of 5 years (60 months), with the option to extend for a further 2 years (24 months), depending on performance and the availability of funding.
Current ring fenced funding is set to 31/3/28 at £2.2m per year, £15,400,000 in total over 7 years.

tender.title: NHS SYICB - Doncaster Place - Mental Health Supported Living Provision
tender.description: Mental health supported living accommodation and recovery-focused support

lots.description:
The provision of mental health supported living service.

NHS SY ICB are intending to award a contract an existing provider following direct award process C.

The approximate lifetime value of the contract is - £5,130,050 based on a 3 year contract, plus the option to extend for a further 2 years.

Please note -the annual value of this contract is£1,026,010 p.a.

The contract will run from 09/11/2026 to 08/11/2029. Additional information: The key criteria were considered in the following ways:

Key Criteria 1
The ICB requires a safe, recovery-focused supported living service for adults with complex mental health needs. The service model must: provide person-centred and least-restrictive support; promote independence, recovery and community inclusion; maintain safeguarding, medicines and regulatory standards; use a stable trained core staff team with management, Quality and Practice Team and Risk Manager support; provide flexible support within the agreed five-band model; and report quality, safety, outcomes, experience and workforce information.

Weighting 30%

Key Criteria 2
Existing packages at Ashmount Court and Magnet Court are paid through spot-purchase arrangements and are reported as 50:50 funded by the ICB and Doncaster Council for Section 117 placements. The provider model flexes temporary changes in support within a fixed weekly fee rather than automatically requesting additional funding. Payments for the two existing sites were reported at approximately £1.026 million per year in total, split equally between the ICB and Doncaster Council, but this must be reconciled with finance records. Positive outcomes have been achieved by service users with good feedback.

Weighting 20%

Key Criteria 3
The service must work as part of Doncaster mental health, social care, housing, Section 117, Continuing Healthcare and discharge pathways. Referrals and funding decisions must be coordinated through the Joint Resource Panel, with clear ICB, Council and provider roles

Lifeways has established supported living provision at Ashmount Court and Magnet Court and has worked with social care referrals and Joint Resource Panel approvals. Existing residents are jointly funded and the ICB currently manages the provider payment, with Council recharge arrangements.

Weighting 25%

Key Criteria 4
The model is person-centred and designed to support people in ordinary community settings who have mental health illnesses. It promotes choice, independence, flexible support and access to health and community services. Referrals to the existing services have mainly been made by Doncaster social care staff, with individual approval through the Joint Resource Panel.

Weighting 15%

Key Criteria 5
The available model describes a trained and supported workforce, reflective practice, management oversight and specialist Quality and Practice Team support. The service supports adults to live in community settings and participate in local life.

Weighting 10%

The Commissioners decided that Lifeways were providing an excellent service and were likely to continue to provide an excellent service in the future.

releases.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The award of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. The publication of this notice marks the start of the standstill period. Representations by providers must be made to the relevant authority by 17th November 2026 23:59. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.

Written representations should be sent to:
Contact: Victoria Sullivan
Email: victoria.sullivan11@nhs.net

Decision-makers:
The decision-makers are recorded as the senior leaders of Barts Health NHS Trust, as follows:
Professor Ian Jacobs, Chair, Barts Health NHS Trust
Decision date: 4th November 2026

Conflicts of interest:
No declared or potential conflicts of interest were identified in the decision-making record.
As no conflicts were identified, no specific conflict-management actions were required.

Relative importance of the key criteria:
The relevant authority considered all five statutory key criteria. In determining relative importance, overall assessments were made on Quality and Innovation and Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability, reflecting the clinical safety, operational resilience and pathway-integration requirements of the Urgent Treatment Centre service, Quality and innovation, Value, integration, collaboration and service sustainability, Improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice and Social value. The decision was based on the overall evidence available, and no criterion was considered in isolation.

Particular importance was placed on:
1 - Quality and innovation: clinical performance, 15-minute assessment, four-hour performance, streaming and governance.
2 - Value: 95% four-hour performance across the combined Type 3 cohort,
reduce first-to-final reporting variation to no more than 5% by the end of 2026/27.
3 - Integration, collaboration and service sustainability: NHS 111, Adastra, local pathways, workforce resilience and overnight provision.
4 - Improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice: accessibility for the Newham population, local-health needs and any evidence concerning inequalities or patient pathways.
5 - Social value: local recruitment and wider community benefits.

This approach reflected the need to appoint a provider capable of delivering a safe, responsive and sustainable urgent treatment service, while supporting access, integration and continuity across local urgent-care pathways.

Rationale for choosing the provider:
PELC was identified as the most suitable provider after consideration of the four identified potential providers. Following application of the basic selection criteria, PELC progressed to assessment against the five statutory key criteria. Following that assessment, PELC was identified as the most suitable provider.
This approach reflected the need to appoint a provider capable of delivering a safe, responsive and sustainable urgent treatment service, while supporting access, integration and continuity across local urgent-care pathways.

PELC provided the strongest overall evidence of established urgent-care delivery. The assessment recorded:
98% four-hour performance, exceeding the 95% service requirement.
99% of patients initially assessed within 15 minutes, exceeding the 95% target.
Existing 24/7 streaming capability and strong overnight coverage.
Established North East London relationships and integration with NHS 111 and Adastra.
Joint operational and governance arrangements with BHRUT.
Wider pathways involving the London Ambulance Service and voluntary-sector partners.
Strong local workforce capability, with more than 70% of staff reported as locally recruited.

On the evidence available, PELC was therefore the strongest overall match against the service requirements and PSR key criteria.

The award remains subject to completion of the standstill period.

Standstill period:
The standstill period begins on the day after publication of this intention to award notice. Written representations may be submitted before midnight at the end of the eighth working day after the standstill period begins.

Standstill period begins: 6th November 2026
Deadline for representations: 17th November 2026 23:59

tender.description:
Barts Health NHS Trust intends to award a contract for the provision of integrated Urgent Treatment Centre services at Newham University Hospital. The services will provide urgent healthcare advice, clinical assessment, treatment, referral, streaming, signposting and associated reporting for patients requiring urgent care.

The provider will be required to deliver safe, effective and responsive urgent care services; integrate with local NHS providers and pathways; maintain sufficient workforce capacity and resilience; and meet the applicable clinical quality, performance, reporting and regulatory standards.

lots.description:
Provision of integrated Urgent Treatment Centre services at Newham University Hospital.

The services include urgent healthcare advice, timely clinical assessment and treatment, streaming, referral and signposting, overnight escalation arrangements, Type 3 urgent care performance, integration with NHS 111 and local urgent-care pathways, and the provision of associated activity, financial, quality, complaints and patient-safety reporting.

The provider will be required to:
Deliver safe, clinically effective and timely assessment and treatment.
Support initial patient assessment within 15 minutes.
Support achievement of the applicable four-hour urgent care performance standard.
Maintain appropriate streaming arrangements, including overnight provision.
Integrate with local NHS providers, pathways and governance arrangements.
Maintain sufficient workforce capacity, resilience and service continuity.
Meet all applicable clinical, quality, performance, reporting and regulatory requirements.

tender.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Secure Patient Transport Services
tender.description:
In 2024, the Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust established a Framework Agreement under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 (and as amended) (the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and
any future successors to these organisations). This is extended to be include the Health Services (Provider Selection Regime)(Wales) Regulations 2025.
"Relevant authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of that Act, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework Agreement.
This framework agreement aims to support mental health patient requirements through the provision of secure patient transport services.
The framework was awarded to run for an initial term of 2 years with options to extend for up to a further 2 years in annual increments. The framework has been extended for 1 year, with one further extension available.
As previously advertised in the Framework tender documentation, the Framework will be reopened to new applicants annually, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date. Previously appointed Suppliers will NOT be obliged to reapply on an annual basis.
Framework Suppliers appointed on the first anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date will be awarded a Framework Agreement of up to 3 years duration; Framework Suppliers appointed on the second anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date will be awarded a Framework Agreement of up to 2 years duration and Framework Suppliers appointed on the third anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date will be awarded a Framework Agreement of up to 1 year duration.
This notice concerns the Second re-opening of the Framework to new applicants.

INTENTION TO AWARD NOTICE for NHS Health Check service Provider Selection Regime - Most Suitable Provider Notice.
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice, under the Most Suitable Provider Process. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to the relevant authority by 17th November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.
The Contracting Authorities intend to award a single contract to the most suitable provider. This is a new service with a new provider and the approximate lifetime value of this contract is £83,800. The dates which the services are intended to be provided are:
Contract Start: 1st January 2027
Contract End: 31st December 2028
The NHS Health Check programme aims to prevent cardiovascular disease (CVD) and associated conditions through the early assessment, awareness, and management of individual behavioural and physiological risk factors. The programme is aimed at all adults in England aged between 40-74 who are not currently being treated for CVD.
The delivery of NHS Health Checks is a statutory responsibility for all Local Authorities (LAs). All eligible individuals must be invited to attend an NHS Health Check once every five years.
The current contract(s) for the delivery of NHS Health Checks lies solely with GP practices across the three LAs. In this financial year, 26/27, all 60 GP Practices across Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire, and Milton Keynes (13 25, 22 respectively) are contracted to deliver NHS Health Checks. However, uptake has remained consistently low for the last five years across all three LAs. In addition, we see lower uptake in more deprived communities, people from minority ethnic backgrounds, and men all of whom tend to access primary care services less frequently.
Low uptake of the NHS Health Check presents a number of risks to each LA, including failing to meet the nationally mandated targets, the inability to identify risk factors for CVD early and therefore missing opportunities for secondary prevention, and a worsening of health inequalities.
A Milton Keynes Primary Care Network (PCN) community outreach offer is required, to supplement GP practice delivery, increase access and enhance the opportunities available for eligible patients to attend for an NHS Health Check at a venue within their own communities and/or within their workplace.
PCNs are well-positioned to deliver this service as they already work closely with, and on behalf of, GP Practices. They have established access to relevant systems and strong working relationships, enabling a seamless pathway for patients to receive an NHS Health Check within a community setting. For efficiencies to the service the expectation is there will be one lead PCN related organisation for contract management purposes and the delivery to the community from the Primary Care Networks.
This approach ensures that, where required, patients can be effectively referred and supported to continue their care through their registered GP Practice following their NHS Health Check. In addition, the service presents an opportunity to build relationships, understanding and trust within communities, encouraging greater engagement with Primary Care services-not only for NHS Health Checks but for a wider range of health interventions.
Those patients who are out of area and whose patient record is not accessible by the provider will receive a paper copy of results and clear instructions to follow up with their own GP Practice
The community outreach offers will support each LA to meet their statutory responsibilities to deliver NHS Health Checks to the eligible population, aged 40-74 on a 5-year rolling basis and reducing health inequalities. It will enable us to meet local and national targets both in the number of NHS Health Checks offered, and those that receive an NHS Health Check.
Who is eligible for an NHS Health Checks in community and workplaces
• 40-74, without an existing diagnosed CVD condition
• Not had an NHS Health Check in the last 5 years
• Resident in Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire and Milton Keynes and/or are registered with a GP practice within Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire and Milton Keynes local authority areas
